outcome: The conjecture was fully proved in 1994 (case A=B, Dias da Silva and Hamidoune, via exterior algebra/representation theory) and 1995 (general case A≠B, Alon–Nathanson–Ruzsa, via the polynomial method), both well before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision. Wikipedia's list entry is simply stale. A 2026 preprint gives a new, more elementary linear-algebraic proof of the already-settled Alon–Nathanson–Ruzsa theorem, which implies the conjecture, but this is a new proof technique for an old result, not new mathematical progress on an open question.
summary: The Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture — that for a prime p and nonempty A ⊆ Z/pZ, the restricted sumset A^A (sums a+a' with a≠a') has size at least min{p, 2|A|-3} — was resolved in two stages entirely before the 26 January 2024 frozen Wikipedia revision. Dias da Silva and Hamidoune proved the case A=B in 1994 in the Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society ('Cyclic spaces for Grassmann derivatives and additive theory'), using exterior/multilinear algebra and representation theory. Alon, Nathanson, and Ruzsa then proved the fully general case (A≠B, restricted sumset A+B with a≠b for the relevant setting) in 1995/1996 using the polynomial method (Combinatorial Nullstellensatz). Both are long-standing, expert-digested results (textbook material in additive combinatorics, e.g. Nathanson's 'Additive Number Theory: Inverse Problems'), so the underlying mathematics is thoroughly resolved and not merely claimed. Searching for any post-January-2024 activity, I found only arXiv:2605.19542 (Guanzhong Yang, submitted 19 May 2026), which gives a new, more elementary linear-algebraic proof (Vandermonde matrices, solvability of linear systems) of the Alon–Nathanson–Ruzsa theorem — i.e., a new route to an already-known result, not a new mathematical fact and not progress on anything still open. I found no AI involvement anywhere in this history: the 2026 paper's abstract and available text describe a purely classical linear-algebra argument with no mention of AI, machine-checked proofs, or LLM assistance. I also checked for any confusion with unrelated 'Erdős' problems making AI news in 2026 (e.g., OpenAI's disproof of the Erdős unit-distance conjecture in discrete geometry) — that is a different, unrelated problem sharing only the Erdős name, and does not touch the Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture. Given the conjecture was fully settled by 1995, the correct status per the rules is open_stale, dated to the first (1994) resolution, with the note that the general case followed in 1995.
competing_reading: One could argue the 'event' should instead point to the 2026 Yang preprint since it is the only item strictly inside the research window. But per §6.1, open_stale exists precisely for problems settled before the frozen revision, and per §3.1 a new proof of an already-settled theorem is not a change to the problem's status — it changes nothing a careful person would write in this bullet's entry, since the bullet asks whether the inequality holds, which was already established. I classify the decisive event as the 1994 (and 1995) resolution and mention the 2026 paper only as context in summary, consistent with the triage's judgment.
what_would_settle_it: Nothing further is needed to settle the mathematics — it is already resolved. What would change this record is discovering that the 2026 (or any other post-2024) paper actually extends the result to a new setting (e.g., non-prime moduli beyond what ANR already covers, or a genuinely new bound), which would make it a 'progress' or 'partial' event instead of stale.
